newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks up ahead of government finance plan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks up ahead of government finance plan.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered from a slow start and shrugged off losses on Wall Street to head towards the psychological 4,000-point barrier in light early afternoon trade on Monday.
Dealers said share prices had gained on selective buying ahead of a financial package to be announced on Tuesday by Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo.
The leading IPC share index was up 27.89 points, or 0.70 percent, at 3,996.70.
The IPC reached a trading record of 4,013.99 on May 23.

"There is little dealing but the market does feel firm. It could well be reacting to the National Development Financing Program (Pronafide). Such buying as there is is selective," a floor trader said.
President Zedillo will unveil the Pronafide on Tuesday, which will set out the government's development strategies up to the year 2000.
Trading volume was just 31.3 million shares, of which an initial public offering accounted for 6.9 million.
On the broad market, of 91 stocks traded, gainers outpaced sliders by 41 to 31.
